explanation: View each array entry as the next-index pointer. Run Floyd’s slow/fast search starting at numbers[0], then reset slow to that same start and advance both one step to the cycle entry.
correctness: The path from index 0 enters a cycle because all links are in 1..n, excluding 0. Its entry has two distinct incoming source indices: the path predecessor and the cycle predecessor. Starting Floyd at numbers[0] removes the first path edge but preserves this entry (or starts directly on it). At a meeting, the faster walker has gained whole cycle lengths; resetting one walker to the chosen start makes equal-speed walkers meet at the entry.
walkthrough: For [4,1,3,4,2], start both walkers at numbers[0]=4. After successive moves (slow,fast) is (2,3), (3,2), then (4,4). Reset slow to 4; the walkers already agree, so return 4. In the full path 0 -> 4 -> 2 -> 3 -> 4, indices 0 and 3 both point to 4, proving it is repeated.
edgeCases: [1,1] returns 1; other valid inputs may contain several duplicate values, so no particular duplicate is mandated.
timeComplexity: O(n) time: Floyd’s meeting phase traverses a prefix and cycle of at most n+1 indices; the entry phase takes at most the prefix length.
spaceComplexity: O(1) auxiliary space: a fixed number of index walkers, with no copied array or visited set.
